draft.title: Sample spaces
card: An experiment is an action with results that are not certain, such as rolling a die or spinning a spinner. Each possible result is an outcome.
The sample space is the list of every possible outcome. We write it inside curly brackets, such as \(\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}\) for one roll of a die.
Each outcome is listed once. Order does not matter, but none can be left out.
Example: a bag holds a red, a blue and a green counter. One counter is taken out. The sample space is \(\{\text{red}, \text{blue}, \text{green}\}\), which has 3 outcomes.
draft.remember: A sample space lists every possible outcome, each one once.

a.q: A coin is tossed once. Which is the sample space?
a.why: A toss can only land heads or tails, and each is listed once. Listing heads twice is wrong because each outcome appears once only.
a.clue: List every result once, with none missing.

b.q: Mia spins a spinner with 5 equal sections numbered 1 to 5. She records the number it lands on. What is the sample space?
b.why: The spinner has sections 1 to 5, so those five numbers are every possible outcome. {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} adds a 6 that is not on the spinner.
b.clue: Only numbers on the spinner can be outcomes.
